reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that persistent code knowledge can be modeled as a layered memory system. At the base layer, a structural map\( \mathcal{M} \) is built using tree-sitter, capturing symbols, imports, and dependencies. This forms a static graph\( \mathcal{G} = (\mathcal{V}, \mathcal{E}) \) where nodes are symbols and edges are dependencies. The second layer uses PageRank to rank module importance, effectively computing a stationary distribution\( \pi \) over\( \mathcal{V} \). The third layer maintains a cache of summaries\( s_i \) for each file\( f_i \), which are updated only when\( h_i \) changes. The key innovation is that\( \mathcal{M} \) enables rapid re-initialization of any agent session through a single\( \texttt{cerebro_map()} \) call, reducing token consumption from\( 100k \) to\( 2–3k \). This is achieved by leveraging the fact that\( \mathcal{M} \) is invariant under repeated calls unless\( \mathcal{H} \) changes. The failure mode arises when\( s_i \) is outdated due to lack of retraining or poor summarization quality, leading to incorrect agent decisions. The system thus balances computational efficiency with semantic fidelity.
